raw: oThe sacred rock at Oda Aboho near Akyim Oda. The three ancestral sisters (Kyekye Ampem, Kyeraa, Ankyaah) are said to have come into existence from the earth beneath this rock. The place is still worshipped and is named Oda Aboho after the condition of the place. This is the mythological origin of the Asankran Kona clan — one of the seven major Akan families.

raw: oEarly ancestor and leader of the Asankran clan. Brother of Anima Kyirisuo. Also known as Nana Kye Buadu I. Came from Asankran with his sister. Died at Gyedua Kankan near the Koto stream during the great migration. Succeeded by Gyapanyin Kyimah. Listed as first chief of the Oda Asankran Branch. The 1990 petition letter confirms: NANA KYE BUADU I led the people from Akim Oda to Wassa Amenfi.

raw: oSister of Kye Boadu. Initially barren; gave birth to first child (Emra Kyereama) through help of a fetish priest. Died in thunderstorm while pregnant with second child (going to fetch fish called Tide). Thereafter named Animah Kyeresuo meaning she who does not like water. Her son Kyi Boadu survived and became head of the family.

raw: oSon of Anima Kyirisuo. Survived when Anima died in the thunderstorm. Became head of the family. Led the great journey — accompanied by grandchildren, slaves and a dog — to find new fertile land. After long journey met Agonahene at Mankaben at Agyakaa; the chief of Bogo allowed them to settle at Gyedua Kankan near the Koto stream.

raw: oSucceeded Kye Boadu as leader. Known as Rover (Kyimah = roaming hunter). Founded the Asankran settlement at Aboman. Met hunter Bruma Ankomah Sono Bofoo at Aboman; took oath to share the forest land marked by a huge silk cotton tree; said me're sankra ha are (I am making complete settlement here) — giving rise to the name Asankran. Listed as second chief of the Oda Asankran Branch. All descendants are called Asankran-fo.
